items.title: KCP in 90 seconds | Migrating from Apache Kafka® to Confluent Cloud
items.author: Confluent Developer
items.summary:
Learn more: https://confluent.io/use-case/kafka-migration/ | Confluent's KCP moves your clients over with no code changes and a cutover window under 30 seconds.

Migrating Kafka clients to Confluent Cloud usually means rewriting client configs, coordinating a big-bang cutover across teams, and hoping the rollback plan works if something breaks. It doesn't have to. KCP, Confluent's open-source CLI, migrates both your Kafka data and Confluent Cloud with zero code changes and a cutover window under 30 seconds. Client apps keep their existing code and credentials: only a bootstrap URL is updated. Cluster Linking replicates topic data and consumer offsets, so consumers pick up in Confluent Cloud exactly where they left off, while producers simply buffer for a few seconds during cutover. KCP groups related topics and clients into "migration groups," so each team migrates on its own schedule instead of a big-bang cutover, and Confluent Cloud Gateway translates credentials behind the scenes so clients keep authenticating the way they always have.

items.title: Data & AI Weekly | Ep. 9 | Why Your AI Agents Need Performance Reviews, Too
items.author: Redpanda Data
items.summary:
Hiring a person comes with a built-in vetting process — resumes, interviews, reference checks — that gives you real confidence they'll behave predictably once they're on the team. Hiring an "agent" skips all of that. You get something capable, sometimes brilliant, with none of the track record.

In this episode, Redpanda Chief Technology Officer, Tyler Akidau sits down with Head of AI, Marc Millstone, to unpack why the enterprises actually getting production value out of agents aren't the fastest movers — they're the ones who can explain, after the fact, exactly what an agent did and why. Drawing on patterns Tyler's seen across dozens of enterprise conversations, they get into what a real evaluation process for an agent looks like, why it has to go well beyond a traditional audit log, and what to get right from day one if you're just getting started.

Now an IBM company, Confluent was built by the creators of Apache Kafka® to help businesses easily access and use live, streaming data. Its platform manages large flows of data and shares them across an organization in real time. Industries like retail, finance, and manufacturing connect their data, analyze it, and run real-time applications. To learn more, please visit https://confluent.io
